$comment: Browserbase's published rates, captured by hand from their pricing page and billing docs. Every figure the comparison page renders comes from here, and the page states capturedOn beside them, because quoting a competitor's prices without a date is how a comparison becomes wrong without anyone touching it. Re-check on the sourceUrl and move capturedOn when it changes.

usage.rate: $0.12 per browser-hour on Developer, $0.10 on Startup
usage.note: Charged once a plan's included hours run out. Billed by the minute, with a one-minute minimum per session.

usage.rate: $12 per GB on Developer, $10 per GB on Startup
usage.note: Billed by the megabyte, with a one-megabyte minimum per session. They publish no separate residential and datacentre rates.
The same rate on Developer and Startup.

usage.rate: $1 per 1,000 calls, or $4 per 1,000 through a proxy
usage.note: One URL per call, no JavaScript execution, and a ten-second timeout.

usage.rate: a monthly allowance, no overage rate published
usage.note: Three a month on Free, 15 on Developer, 50 on Startup. The model behind them is not disclosed.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: 1 browser hour, no proxy bandwidth, 3 agent runs, sessions capped at 15 minutes, 7-day data retention

plans.name: Developer
plans.note: 100 browser hours, 1GB of proxy bandwidth, 15 agent runs, basic stealth, 7-day data retention

plans.name: Startup
plans.note: 500 browser hours, 5GB of proxy bandwidth, 50 agent runs, basic stealth, 30-day data retention

plans.name: Scale
plans.note: Custom pricing. 250 concurrent browsers or more, advanced stealth, verified agents, SSO, HIPAA and a DPA on request

billingNote: Browser time is billed by the minute and proxy bandwidth by the megabyte, each with a one-unit minimum per session.
annualNote: No annual billing is published. The pricing page lists monthly rates only.
unverifiedNote: Two things could not be confirmed on the pricing page itself and are therefore not quoted here: an Extract API overage rate that appeared once and could not be re-isolated, and the session-length caps on the paid tiers, which appear only in the plans-and-pricing documentation. Scale publishes no rate for anything.
